Still: Amortized KV Cache Compaction in a Single Forward Pass

Charles O’Neill ††thanks: First author. Affiliation: Baseten Affiliation: San Francisco Email: charlie.oneill@baseten.co    Alex Sandomirsky11footnotemark: 1 Affiliation: Baseten Affiliation: San Francisco Email: alex.sandomirsky@baseten.co    Harry Partridge11footnotemark: 1 Affiliation: Baseten Affiliation: San Francisco Email: harry.partridge@baseten.co    Mudith Jayasekara Affiliation: Baseten Affiliation: San Francisco Email: mudith@baseten.co    Max Kirkby Affiliation: Baseten Affiliation: London Email: max.kirkby@baseten.co
Abstract

The KV cache is the memory bottleneck of long-horizon language model deployment. Practically, a deployable compactor must be lightweight enough to call during inference, expressive enough to preserve context under constraint, and reusable across a trajectory. Existing compaction methods satisfy only part of this requirement: selection methods are lightweight but subset-bound, while synthesis methods are expressive but rely on per-context optimization. Here we introduce Still, a small per-layer Perceiver trained once against a frozen base model that produces compact keys and values in a single forward pass. On Qwen and Gemma models, Still occupies the favorable side of the speed–quality frontier across compression ratios from 8×8\times to 200×200\times and context lengths from 88k to 128128k. On the long-context RULER grid, Still exceeds the strongest baseline by 8–22 points. The same compact cache also supports free-form summarization, preserving most of the full-context gain on HELMET and winning a pairwise LongBench summarization comparison against KV-Distill. Because compaction is a forward pass, Still can be applied iteratively, entering a long-horizon regime unavailable to per-context methods. We show that amortization makes long-context cache compaction tractable, and synthesis makes its compact state useful at extreme compression.

1 Introduction

The KV cache is the memory bottleneck of long-horizon language model deployment (Kwon et al., 2023). As LLMs operate over multi-day coding agents, multi-turn tool use, and repository-scale reasoning, the cache becomes the binding constraint on what these systems can do. Today’s options are an all-or-nothing choice: a lossless cache that grows linearly with context length, or lossy alternatives (fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, document summaries) that abandon the structure and fidelity of the model’s own internal representations.

KV cache compaction has emerged as the central primitive for managing this gap, with existing methods falling along two axes: the compact cache is either selected from original tokens or synthesized via content-dependent combination, and the work is performed per-context at inference, amortized once offline, or trained-in as part of pretraining. Per-context selection (Zhang et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Cai et al., 2025; Kim et al., 2025) scores tokens on the fly and evicts the rest, which is lightweight but structurally subset-bound. Per-context synthesis (Eyuboglu et al., 2025; Zweiger et al., 2026) lifts this ceiling but requires optimization for each context. Amortized selection appeared recently in KV-Distill (Chari et al., 2025), which produces a subset of original tokens in a single prefill via a learned scorer plus LoRA (Hu et al., 2022) adaptors.

We study the underexplored combination of amortized synthesis of layer-wise KV caches for frozen pretrained models. This targets plug-in compaction of existing open-weight checkpoints, with synthesis avoiding the subset problem of token selection and amortization avoiding per-context optimization. Representation learning reaches the same conclusion in analogous settings: amortized variational inference (Kingma and Welling, 2014; Rezende et al., 2014) and sparse autoencoders (Makhzani and Frey, 2014; Bricken et al., 2023) both replace repeated per-instance optimization over a fixed structure with a learned encoder. In each case, the lesson has been to learn the optimizer. We apply the same move to KV-cache synthesis.

We introduce Still, a small Perceiver-based (Jaegle et al., 2021; Alayrac et al., 2022) compactor for this setting (Figure 1). Still consists of one module per transformer layer; each maintains a bank of learned latent queries that cross-attends the full KV cache and produce compact keys and values in a single forward pass, all without reference queries, gradient steps, or closed-form solves at inference. Empirically, we evaluate Still as a compaction primitive across four regimes: the single-pass speed–quality frontier across compression ratios and contexts (§3.1), transfer of these traits across model scales and attention architectures (§3.2), long-context evidence preservation against amortized selection together with free-form summarization (§3.3, §3.5), and iterative chunked compaction at a fixed compression ratio (§3.4).

In the sweep on Qwen3-4B (Qwen Team, 2025), Still occupies the favorable side of the speed–quality frontier across 8×8\times–200×200\times compression and 88k–6464k contexts (Figure 2). Comparable methods that are accurate at low compression are slow, and methods that are fast lose accuracy under tight budgets; Still is the only evaluated method that remains both accurate and fast across the matrix. The same recipe transfers across Qwen3 dense models from 4B to 32B, the Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE, and Gemma-3’s (Gemma Team, 2025) mixed sliding-window/global attention stack.

At long context, the matched-training RULER (Hsieh et al., 2024) Still exceeds KV-Distill by 88–2222 accuracy points across 16 of 18 matched-training cells. The compact cache also supports free-form summarization. On HELMET (Yen et al., 2025) multi_lexsum (Shen et al., 2022), Still preserves most of the full-context summarization gain across 88k–6464k contexts while compressing the document prefix before generation, and remains ahead of Attention Matching and KV-Distill at every length. On LongBench v1 (Bai et al., 2024a) GovReport and QMSum, Still also wins 60%60\% of pairwise judge comparisons against KV-Distill (§3.5). Because Still is a forward pass, it can be called repeatedly as new context arrives, and we show that this enables iterative chunked compaction at a fixed compression ratio. This is the setting in which per-context synthesis is least practical, since its fitting cost compounds with every compaction event.

Together, Still is a learned primitive that uses amortization to create a compact cache that across several axes may be usable at inference time.

2 Method

Let fθf_{\theta} be a frozen autoregressive transformer with LL layers, HH KV-heads per layer, head dimension dd, and rotary position embeddings (Su et al., 2023). Given a prefix of TT tokens, fθf_{\theta} produces a per-layer KV cache; for layer ℓ\ell and KV-head hh, write the cached keys and values as K(ℓ,h),V(ℓ,h)∈ℝT×dK^{(\ell,h)},V^{(\ell,h)}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d}. Still learns a per-layer compactor

gϕ(ℓ):(K(ℓ,h),V(ℓ,h))h=1H↦(Ck(ℓ,h),Cv(ℓ,h))h=1H,g_{\phi}^{(\ell)}:(K^{(\ell,h)},V^{(\ell,h)})_{h=1}^{H}\mapsto(C_{k}^{(\ell,h)},C_{v}^{(\ell,h)})_{h=1}^{H},

with Ck(ℓ,h),Cv(ℓ,h)∈ℝt×dC_{k}^{(\ell,h)},C_{v}^{(\ell,h)}\in\mathbb{R}^{t\times d}, and t≪Tt\ll T. The compact cache replaces the original prefix cache when running fθf_{\theta} on subsequent tokens. The implementation also supports the optional log-space bias channel used by Attention Matching (Zweiger et al., 2026), but that channel is disabled for the reported Still results. The base model’s weights are unchanged. We describe a single layer below and suppress the layer index where unambiguous.

2.1 Per-layer Perceiver compactor

Still uses one Perceiver-style compactor per transformer layer (Jaegle et al., 2021; Alayrac et al., 2022). Within a layer, the compactor operates on all HH KV-heads jointly: each head has its own bank of tt learned latent queries Z∈ℝH×t×dℓZ\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times t\times d_{\ell}}, while linear projections are shared across heads.

The input to a layer’s compactor is the per-head concatenation X(h)=[K(h);V(h)]∈ℝT×2​dX^{(h)}=[K^{(h)};V^{(h)}]\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times 2d}, with cached keys first un-rotated into a position-free frame (§2.2). The latents pass through BB pre-norm blocks; a block applies cross-attention from the latents into XX ie., Z′=Z+CrossAttn⁡(RMSNorm⁡(Z),X)Z^{\prime}=Z+\mathrm{CrossAttn}(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Z),X), latent self-attention Z′′=Z′+SelfAttn⁡(RMSNorm⁡(Z′))Z^{\prime\prime}=Z^{\prime}+\mathrm{SelfAttn}(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Z^{\prime})), and an optional position-wise feed-forward sublayer Z′′′=Z′′+FFN⁡(RMSNorm⁡(Z′′))Z^{\prime\prime\prime}=Z^{\prime\prime}+\mathrm{FFN}(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Z^{\prime\prime})) (norms are RMSNorm (Zhang and Sennrich, 2019)). Two independent linear heads, shared across KV-heads within a layer, project the final latent state ZoutZ_{\mathrm{out}} to compact keys Ck=Zout​WkeyC_{k}=Z_{\mathrm{out}}W_{\mathrm{key}}, compact values Cv=Zout​WvalC_{v}=Z_{\mathrm{out}}W_{\mathrm{val}}. An optional third head can produce per-token biases β=Zout​wβ\beta=Z_{\mathrm{out}}w_{\beta}, but reported experiments set β=0\beta=0. The only per-KV-head parameters are the latent banks. For global-attention layers the compact (Ck,Cv)(C_{k},C_{v}) replace the full prefix cache; for architectures with mixed sliding-window and global attention (e.g. Gemma-3), Still applies compaction only to global-attention layers.

Canonical configuration.

Throughout the paper we hold the Still architecture fixed and vary only the compact length tt. The canonical configuration on Qwen3-4B uses dℓ=256d_{\ell}=256 and B=2B=2 blocks with cross-attention repeated in every block; at t=128t=128 this is roughly 5050M parameters, around 1%1\% of the base model.11 1 Architecture sweeps (§M) show that headline accuracy is insensitive to most architectural choices; the binding constraint is within-layer coordination, not capacity. Full hyperparameters (nc,nsn_{c},n_{s} heads, FFN setting, QK-norm and logit scale, RoPE base, and optional β\beta support) and the detailed cross-attention math are in Appendix A.

2.2 Position-free compaction

The base model’s cached keys are already RoPE-rotated (Su et al., 2023), so the same content has different key vectors at different positions. Forcing the compactor to synthesize mixtures of already-rotated keys mixes content with phase and is empirically unstable. Still therefore operates in a position-free frame: cached keys are inverse-rotated before the compactor, the compactor uses its own RoPE inside cross-attention with latent queries placed at evenly spaced positions over the compacted range, and the resulting compact keys are re-rotated at chosen output positions before being written into the cache. Values are not rotated. We use an identity-style initialization that makes the compactor a near-pass-through map at t=Tt=T; it requires dℓ=2​dd_{\ell}=2d and is described in Appendix C.

2.3 Single-pass and iterative compaction

Single-pass compaction.

For a static prefix, Still runs the frozen base model once to obtain the full per-layer KV cache, applies the per-layer compactors to that cache, and substitutes the resulting (Ck,Cv)(C_{k},C_{v}) for the original prefix entries. The continuation path (question, generation, or downstream tokens) is processed against the compact prefix unchanged, with continuation positions offset so that RoPE phases on new tokens behave as if the full original prefix were still present.

Iterative chunked compaction.

For long-horizon settings where context arrives over time, Still supports a recurrent schedule with fixed local compression ratio cc. Pass 0 prefills the first 2​c​t2ct tokens and then compacts the first c​tct KV entries to tt entries. Each subsequent pass N>0N>0 prefills the next outstanding chunk of c​tct tokens, conditioned on the NN already compacted KV chunks concatenated with a raw KV chunk. In other words, the base model at pass NN sees a KV cache of length (N+c)​t(N+c)t, and uses this to prefill the next c​tct tokens. The chunk of c​tct tokens preceding this newly prefilled one is then compacted to tt entries. The retained cache after ingesting TT tokens is therefore T/c+c​tT/c+ct entries: linear in context at compression rate 1/c1/c, rather than constant. This is a fixed local compression ratio with bounded per-chunk growth, not a constant absolute budget; we discuss truly constant-budget recurrences as an open direction in §5.

It is crucial for prefill to occur sequentially this way in tandem with compaction because this matches the use case at inference over long contexts. We provide a one chunk buffer of raw KV cache at every prefill because it prevents infidelity of the compaction from compounding too aggressively. We refer to this buffering mechanism as lookahead. Compact-key re-rotation, position-offset accounting, and the chunked-prefill / lookahead pipeline used as the default for iterative results are in Appendix B.

2.4 Training

Data.

The canonical training corpus is a four-domain extractive multiple-choice QA dataset spanning Financial filings, Project Gutenberg literature, Legal documents, and Code, with each example a triple of (long-context prefill, MCQ prompt, answer-letter target). Questions are generated from random sub-chunks of the prefill, verified by the same frozen base model used as teacher, and filtered to remove items the base model can answer without the context. Domains are downsampled to the smallest, giving ∼120\sim 120k items and ∼1\sim 1B context tokens at 88k context length; 1616k single-pass and {8​k,16​k,32​k}\{8\text{k},16\text{k},32\text{k}\} iterative families use matched splits prepared the same way. Per-domain item counts are in Appendix E.

Training.

The training signal is forward KL divergence from a full-context teacher to the compact-cache student, masked to answer-side tokens only:

ℒ=𝔼(c,p,a)∼𝒟∑i∈ansKL(fθ(⋅∣c,p,a<i)∥fθ(⋅∣gϕ(c),p,a<i)),\mathcal{L}=\mathbb{E}_{(c,p,a)\sim\mathcal{D}}\sum_{i\in\mathrm{ans}}\mathrm{KL}\!\left(f_{\theta}(\cdot\mid c,p,a_{<i})\,\|\,f_{\theta}(\cdot\mid g_{\phi}(c),p,a_{<i})\right),

where teacher and student are the same frozen base model differing only in whether the prefix cache is the full uncompressed cache or Still’s compact cache. Answer tokens consist of a rationale trace followed by the MCQ answer token to provide a richer feedback signal than what would be available from just the single MCQ answer token. The KL is evaluated on the top 200200 teacher-vocabulary tokens with the gold answer token forced into the support, which keeps the loss memory-bounded; Appendix F validates this choice by finding no gain from top-10001000 or full-vocabulary support under a common full-vocabulary evaluation. The compactor parameters ϕ\phi are the only trainable parameters; θ\theta remains frozen throughout. Cache-MSE and residual variants are ablations only (Appendix M.3). Except for the explicitly labeled generation-aligned LongBench summarization checkpoint in §3.5, paper-facing Still checkpoints use pure KL.

We train with AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019) at learning rate 4×10−54\times 10^{-5} on 8×8\times H200 with DDP at effective batch 3232, taking all Qwen3-4B checkpoints at training step 15001500. Full hyperparameters (weight decay, warmup, schedule, gradient clipping) are in Appendix E.

We report mean (SD) over 33 training seeds for all frontier results (Table 8, Figure 15, Figure 2, Figure 16). Deterministic baselines (H2O, SnapKV, StreamingLLM, Attention Matching, AM-OMP-fast) are seed-invariant; their reported SD is bootstrap over evaluation examples. The RULER cells (§3.3) and the RULER and LongBench v2 rows of the Still-vs-KV-Distill summary (Table 9) are reported as 3-seed means with seed-level SDs. HELMET (§3.5), iterative-compaction (§3.4), and the QuALITY-derived row of Table 9 remain single-seed with bootstrap-over-examples SDs, and we flag this in those sections.

2.5 Baselines

We compare Still against representative methods from the populated regions of this design space. Per-context selection: H2O (Zhang et al., 2023) retains tokens by cumulative attention scores from extracted reference queries; SnapKV (Li et al., 2024) scores tokens within a 6464-token observation window with a 55-token pooling kernel; StreamingLLM (Xiao et al., 2024) keeps 44 attention-sink tokens plus the most recent K−4K-4 tokens. Per-context synthesis: Attention Matching (Zweiger et al., 2026) uses repeat-prefill query extraction, top-kk key selection by RMS score, least-squares value reconstruction, and nonnegative least-squares β\beta fitting. Amortized selection: KV-Distill (Chari et al., 2025) uses a learned token scorer with top-kk retention, rank-128128 LoRA adaptors on Q,K,V,OQ,K,V,O, and forced sink tokens with an uncompressed question/answer path. Each baseline runs a single configuration across all evaluations, with only the cache budget KK varying to match Still’s compression ratio. Implementation details, including the KV-Distill retraining protocol and Attention Matching’s reference-query budget, are in Appendix G.

3 Results

Each subsection asks where Still sits relative to populated alternatives in the cache-compaction design space. We report the speed–quality frontier across compression ratios and context lengths (§3.1), transfer to other model scales and to a mixed sliding-window/global attention stack (§3.2), long-context behavior against the strongest amortized-selection baseline (§3.3), iterative compaction at a fixed compression ratio (§3.4), and free-form generation (§3.5).

3.1 Amortized synthesis offers the best speed–quality tradeoff across the design space

We sweep compression ratios from 8×8\times to 200×200\times across 8​k,16​k,32​k,64​k{8\text{k},16\text{k},32\text{k},64\text{k}} contexts, comparing Still with per-context selection methods (H2O, SnapKV, StreamingLLM), per-context synthesis (Attention Matching), amortized selection (KV-Distill), and a prompted natural-language summarization baseline. The main result is the frontier shape (Figure 2): selection methods degrade under tight budgets, prompted summaries preserve some question-relevant content but pass through a lossy text bottleneck, and Still is the only method that remains accurate across the sweep. We also ran a targeted partial KVZip comparison at 88k and 1616k because it is the closest recent query-agnostic neighbor; Appendix J.1 reports the results and why we do not treat that reference-port check as a full-matrix baseline. A 256k-token single-pass Still compactor at 100× compression reaches 40.7% (3-seed σ=3.2\sigma=3.2) compact accuracy on a QuALITY-concat diagnostic, with full-context (55%, σ=1.8\sigma=1.8) and no-context (22%, σ=1.5\sigma=1.5), showing the same mechanism can be trained directly at much longer contexts. All frontier numbers in Figure 2, Table 8, and Figure 16 are means over 33 training seeds for the learned methods (Still, KV-Distill); RULER (§3.3) is also reported as 3-seed means with seed-level SDs, while HELMET (§3.5) and iterative compaction (§3.4) are reported single-seed with bootstrap-over-examples SDs.

3.2 The same compactor transfers across model scales and attention architectures

Holding architecture, training corpus, optimizer, schedule, and compactor depth fixed, Figure 4 reports compact-cache utility across the Qwen3 dense family from 4B to 32B with the 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts on the same plot (left), and on Gemma-3 4B’s mixed sliding-window/global attention stack (right). Across the Qwen3 dense models the compact cache stays usefully inside the no-context-to-full-context band at every size; the MoE transfers without modification, since the compact-cache interface is determined by attention-layer KV geometry and FFN structure is not part of that interface. Gemma-3 transfers under a single specialization i.e., compact only the global-attention layers, leaving sliding-window layers (which already have a bounded cache) untouched with β=0\beta=0. This recipe matches or exceeds every fixed-cache baseline on Gemma-3 4B at 16k.

3.3 Long-context generalization against amortized selection

The cleanest comparison between amortized synthesis and amortized selection is at matched training and matched evaluation. Figure 5(a) reports compactors trained directly on RULER tasks and evaluated on held-out RULER tasks at 32k/64k/128k; Figure 5(b) reports the more demanding transfer setting from the mixed-domain MCQ corpus. We include LongBench v2 (Bai et al., 2024b) (a 4-way multiple-choice benchmark, distinct from the LongBench v1 free-form summarization audit in §3.5) in Table 9 as an additional transfer diagnostic.

Under matched training, Still exceeds KV-Distill by 88–2222 accuracy points in 16 of 18 cells. The two exceptions (64k/K=82K{=}82 and 128k/K=82K{=}82) sit within seed-level noise, isolating the failure regime as long context combined with extreme compression. The transfer setting tells the same qualitative story with smaller margins; the within-noise region extends to a handful of additional cells at K≤164K\leq 164 on 128k as the train–test mismatch tax compounds with proximity to the no-context floor. Per-cell 3-seed means and seed-level SDs are in Table 12.

3.4 Iterative compaction at fixed compression ratio

In long-horizon settings, context arrives over time and the deployment constraint is a fixed compression ratio: the retained cache grows with the trajectory at rate 1/c1/c rather than at full token rate, with bounded per-chunk overhead. Per-context synthesis methods are operationally unattractive in this regime because their per-invocation optimization compounds across the trajectory. With Still, mid-trajectory compaction is a forward pass. All iterative results in this section use β=0\beta=0.

Figure 6 evaluates iterative chunked compaction (§2.3) on Long-MCQ, comparing Still checkpoints trained at three iterative horizons (8k, 16k, 32k) deployed at 32k, 64k, and 128k. Each checkpoint produces t=128t=128 latents per chunk at a fixed per-chunk compression ratio cc tied to its training horizon: 10241024-token chunks at c=8c=8 (8k-trained), 20482048-token chunks at c=16c=16 (16k-trained), and 40964096-token chunks at c=32c=32 (32k-trained). All cells use the lookahead variant (one-chunk raw-KV buffer, Appendix B); the number of stacked compaction passes ranges from 88 (32k-trained at 32k) to 128128 (8k-trained at 128k). The 8k-trained compactor reaches 51.0%51.0\% at 32k but collapses to 1.5%1.5\% at 128k, below the no-context floor; training on longer iterative contexts removes this collapse, with the 16k-trained checkpoint reaching 35.2%35.2\% and the 32k-trained checkpoint 39.2%39.2\% at 128k, with the same pattern reflected in utilization. The collapse is not a cache-budget effect: by the recurrence accounting in §2.3, the 8k-trained checkpoint retains a larger cache at 128k (1740817408 slots) than the 32k-trained one (81928192); the binding constraint is the training horizon, since the 8k checkpoint never saw 128128 stacked compactions during training. Additional dataset and task diagnostics, including QuALITY and RULER iterative sweeps and the evaluation-mode ablation, are in Appendix O.

3.5 Free-form summarization preserves most of the full-context gain

HELMET summarization asks whether the compact cache can support free-form summarization rather than only answer selection. Table 1 reports Still, Attention Matching (AM), and KV-Distill on multi_lexsum, where each summary is scored by HELMET’s GPT-4o judge against full-context and no-context references. Across 8k–64k contexts, Still recovers 7474–95%95\% of the full-context gain while compressing the document prefix before generation, and it still recovers 59%59\% at 128k. AM and KV-Distill both lag Still at every context length, with the gap to KV-Distill widening from ∼9\sim 9 points at 8k to nearly 1616 points by 128k, the same ordering observed on matched-training RULER (§3.3).

LongBench v1 (Bai et al., 2024a) (open-ended summarization; distinct from the LongBench v2 multiple-choice transfer diagnostic in §3.3) asks for direct open-ended summarization rather than normalized utilization against full- and no-context anchors. Table 2 reports a held-out GovReport/QMSum comparison between Still and KV-Distill at the same 16k context and K=1024K=1024 retained-cache budget. Both checkpoints are short generation-aligned continuations of their respective 16k/K=1024K{=}1024 checkpoints, trained on GovReport/QMSum summary rows under the identical recipe; sampling, training, and judge details are in Appendix K. Still wins 300300 of 500500 pairwise comparisons and improves the mean GPT-5.5 judge score by 5.45.4 points.

4 Related Work

The KV cache compaction literature (Kwon et al., 2023) spans selection and synthesis methods with per-context, amortized, or trained-in computation. Per-context selection methods (Zhang et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Cai et al., 2025; Xiao et al., 2024; Kim et al., 2025) score tokens at inference and evict the rest; the compact entries must be rows of the original cache, so the cell’s quality ceiling falls with the input’s information density. The remaining regions are populated more sparsely, and we compare Still against a representative method from each.

KV-Distill (Chari et al., 2025) is the closest published neighbor: a learned scorer identifies tokens to retain via top-kk, and rank-128128 LoRA adaptors on the base model’s Q,K,V,OQ,K,V,O matrices route retained tokens through trainable projections during a modified prefill, trained with symmetric KL against the uncompressed-cache teacher. Each compact entry remains a row of the original cache; the LoRA paths modulate how attention reads the cache rather than what it contains. Still inherits the amortization move but breaks the selection constraint — a single Still slot can blend information from arbitrarily many positions via cross-attention — and leaves the base model’s weights unchanged. The cell-level gap (§3.3) widens with both context length and compression ratio.

The strongest quality references in the literature compact in latent space rather than by selection. Cartridges (Eyuboglu et al., 2025) treats the compact cache as a parameter and trains it via prefix tuning (Li and Liang, 2021) on synthetic “self-study” interactions generated by the base model; structural analysis of trained Cartridges (Diaz, 2025) finds that the keys act as stable retrieval routers while values carry most of the compressed content. Attention Matching (Zweiger et al., 2026) preserves attention outputs and per-head attention mass via closed-form key selection, least-squares value reconstruction, and nonnegative least-squares fitting of per-token biases. Still inherits the latent-space synthesis paradigm from this line, supports the same optional bias interface for diagnostics, and removes per-context optimization from the reported method: compaction is a single forward pass through a learned module, which is the operational distinction that enables iterative long-horizon compaction (§3.4).

A separate axis reduces cache cost by changing the model itself, from grouped-query attention (Ainslie et al., 2023) and Dynamic Memory Compression (Nawrot et al., 2024) to multi-head latent attention (DeepSeek-AI, 2024) and native sparse attention (Yuan et al., 2025). The most sophisticated synthesis-based instance is DeepSeek-V4 (DeepSeek-AI, 2026), which interleaves softmax-gated pooling, sparse top-kk block selection, and a sliding-window path. Still and V4 both synthesize compact entries rather than selecting original tokens, but V4 bakes compression into pretraining over a fixed local receptive field, whereas Still trains a small module against a frozen checkpoint with global cross-attention; the convergence on synthesis is independent evidence for the design choice.

Still’s architecture is a small Perceiver (Jaegle et al., 2021), closest in application to the Perceiver Resampler in Flamingo (Alayrac et al., 2022), which distils variable-length visual features into a fixed token budget for language-model conditioning. Earlier context-compression work (Mu et al., 2023; Chevalier et al., 2023; Ge et al., 2024) uses related token-bottleneck ideas but operates in input or activation space rather than producing layer-wise compact KV caches.

5 Discussion

The iterative-compaction result in §3.4 cuts both ways. The 16k- and 32k-trained compactors absorb context many times their physical capacity at 128k, but the 8k-trained compactor collapses below the no-context floor and the 32k-trained compactor still degrades meaningfully from 32k to 128k. Iterative compaction is not free extrapolation; the failure is graceful only within the trained range. Supporting deployment at, say, 1M tokens therefore requires training at iterative horizons proportionally longer than 16k or 32k, which is expensive both in token count and in the difficulty of curating long-context training data. Curriculum schedules over horizon, training Still directly under the recurrence, and constant-budget variants that reuse or merge compact slots in place are all natural follow-ups. The optional β\beta-scaling diagnostic in Appendix M illustrates why this matters: post-hoc calibration that looks reasonable in single-pass compaction can become miscalibrated under recurrence, even though the reported Still results avoid that deployment knob by setting β=0\beta=0. Once compaction itself is cheap, the binding constraint shifts to training a compactor whose distribution covers the lengths and intermediate cache states it will encounter at deployment.

HELMET multi_lexsum and LongBench v1 summarization (§3.5) extend this from answer selection to free-form summarization. The compact cache is a usable conditioning state for the frozen base model in both retrieving evidence under multiple-choice scoring and for generating summaries from a compressed document prefix. The comparison to KV-Distill is precisely useful because both methods are amortized, but KV-Distill can only retain original cache rows whereas Still can synthesize compact entries. This supports an interpretation of a compressed working memory that the model can attend to natively, without lossless recall of every original token. Critically, this does not establish arbitrary open-ended generation or exact recall.

The matched-training RULER result gives the cleanest comparison, as we fix the training distribution and change the compaction cell from amortized selection to amortized synthesis. The transfer cells ask a harder question, whether the learned compact state remains useful when the task moves away from training. The smaller margins we observe there, and the occasional approach to parity (Table 9), are therefore best read as a train–test mismatch rather than a reversal of the main result. Clearly, scaling Still will require training mixtures that cover the task surfaces on which the compact cache is expected to operate.

Limitations.

Still is not lossless: full-context inference remains substantially better in the hardest 128k settings, and iterative compaction is not free extrapolation because the training horizon strongly affects where repeated compression breaks down. The iterative recurrence as described here also holds only a fixed compression ratio rather than a constant absolute cache budget — the retained cache grows linearly with trajectory length at rate 1/c1/c — so the long-horizon regime we report is one of bounded per-chunk growth, not O⁡(1)O(1) recurrent memory; an in-place slot-reuse variant is left to future work. The current recurrence also remains weak on exact-retrieval and needle-style tasks, even when it preserves enough semantic evidence for broader MCQ-style evaluations, and most headline results are still extractive multiple-choice rather than open-ended deployment workloads. Operationally, single-pass Still runs after a full prefill of the original prefix, so in that mode it reduces the retained cache and subsequent attention cost rather than eliminating the initial full-context pass; iterative chunked compaction (§2.3) avoids the full-prefix pass by ingesting context in chunks, but inherits the training-horizon constraints above. Each base checkpoint also needs its own trained compactor, adding parameters, training data requirements, and training cost. Finally, although our implementation supports an optional per-token bias channel, the reported Still results use β=0\beta=0; enabling such biases in production would require attention-kernel support or a slower custom path.

6 Conclusion

Still is a learned KV-state transform that is lightweight enough to call repeatedly, expressive enough to beat token selection when information density is high, stable enough to transfer across model scales and attention architectures, and useful enough to support both answer selection and free-form summarization. Amortization makes cache compaction tractable at long context; in the regimes we evaluate, synthesis gives the compact state enough expressive capacity to be worth amortizing.

Appendix A Architecture Details

This appendix expands the per-layer compactor description in §2.1. The notation follows the main text: dd is the base model’s KV head dimension, HH the number of KV-heads per layer, dℓd_{\ell} the compactor latent dimension, tt the compact length, BB the block count, and nc,nsn_{c},n_{s} the cross- and self-attention head counts.

Input concatenation and RoPE handling.

For a single layer and KV-head, keys and values are concatenated along the feature axis:

X(h)=[K(h);V(h)]∈ℝT×2​d,h=1,…,H.X^{(h)}=[K^{(h)};V^{(h)}]\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times 2d},\qquad h=1,\ldots,H.

When RoPE-fix is enabled (the canonical setting), cached keys are first un-rotated into a position-free frame before this concatenation; values are not rotated.

Latent queries.

Each layer maintains learned latents Z∈ℝH×t×dℓZ\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times t\times d_{\ell}}. The first axis indexes KV-heads, so each head receives its own bank of tt latents; linear projections are shared across heads. Sharing the projections gives the compactor an implicit per-head budget without the parameter blowup that per-head projections would incur. The canonical initialiser is the block-diagonal identity-style construction of Appendix C; random and orthogonal initialisers are supported as ablations.

Compactor blocks.

The compactor contains BB pre-norm blocks. The standard Perceiver-resampler setting applies cross-attention only in the first block; the canonical Still configuration applies cross-attention in every block. Self-attention and the feed-forward sublayer are independently configurable. With RMSNorm\mathrm{RMSNorm} denoting non-parametric RMSNorm [Zhang and Sennrich, 2019], a block with all three sublayers computes

Z′\displaystyle Z^{\prime} =Z+CrossAttn⁡(RMSNorm⁡(Z),X),\displaystyle=Z+\mathrm{CrossAttn}(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Z),X), (1)
Z′′\displaystyle Z^{\prime\prime} =Z′+SelfAttn⁡(RMSNorm⁡(Z′)),\displaystyle=Z^{\prime}+\mathrm{SelfAttn}(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Z^{\prime})), (2)
Z′′′\displaystyle Z^{\prime\prime\prime} =Z′′+FFN⁡(RMSNorm⁡(Z′′)).\displaystyle=Z^{\prime\prime}+\mathrm{FFN}(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Z^{\prime\prime})). (3)

Disabled sublayers omit their residual update; blocks after the first in the Perceiver-resampler setting apply only the enabled latent self-attention and feed-forward updates.

Cross-attention.

Cross-attention is multi-head with ncn_{c} heads. We use the convention that the expanded model dimension is nc​dℓn_{c}d_{\ell}, so each attention head has dimension dℓd_{\ell} rather than dℓ/ncd_{\ell}/n_{c}: multi-head fan-out widens the projection dimension and the output projection contracts back to the latent backbone width. The cross-attention inputs are the RMSNorm’d latent bank Q=RMSNorm⁡(Z)∈ℝt×dℓQ=\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Z)\in\mathbb{R}^{t\times d_{\ell}} (per KV-head, with projections shared across KV-heads) and the per-head concatenated cache X=[K;V]∈ℝT×2​dX=[K;V]\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times 2d}. For head ii,

q~i\displaystyle\tilde{q}_{i} =Q​WQi+bQi,\displaystyle=QW_{Q_{i}}+b_{Q_{i}}, WQi\displaystyle W_{Q_{i}} ∈ℝdℓ×dℓ,\displaystyle\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\ell}\times d_{\ell}}, bQi\displaystyle b_{Q_{i}} ∈ℝdℓ,\displaystyle\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\ell}}, (4)
k~i\displaystyle\tilde{k}_{i} =X​WKi+bKi,\displaystyle=XW_{K_{i}}+b_{K_{i}}, WKi\displaystyle W_{K_{i}} ∈ℝ2​d×dℓ,\displaystyle\in\mathbb{R}^{2d\times d_{\ell}}, bKi\displaystyle b_{K_{i}} ∈ℝdℓ,\displaystyle\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\ell}}, (5)
vi\displaystyle v_{i} =X​WVi,\displaystyle=XW_{V_{i}}, WVi\displaystyle W_{V_{i}} ∈ℝ2​d×dℓ.\displaystyle\in\mathbb{R}^{2d\times d_{\ell}}. (6)

The query and key projections carry additive biases; the value projection does not. Queries and keys are L2L_{2}-normalized after the linear projection but before the dot product [Dehghani et al., 2023, QK-norm;]. When cross-attention positions are supplied, the compactor applies its own RoPE to the normalized queries and keys:

qi\displaystyle q_{i} =RoPE⁡(NormL2​(q~i),𝐩(q)),\displaystyle=\mathrm{RoPE}\!\left(\mathrm{Norm}_{L_{2}}(\tilde{q}_{i}),\mathbf{p}^{(q)}\right), (7)
ki\displaystyle k_{i} =RoPE⁡(NormL2​(k~i),𝐩(k)).\displaystyle=\mathrm{RoPE}\!\left(\mathrm{Norm}_{L_{2}}(\tilde{k}_{i}),\mathbf{p}^{(k)}\right). (8)

Key positions 𝐩(k)\mathbf{p}^{(k)} are the input cache positions; latent query positions 𝐩(q)\mathbf{p}^{(q)} are evenly spaced between the first and last supplied key positions. The compactor RoPE base is a hyperparameter (canonical value 1010) and can optionally be learned per dimension.

After QK-norm the raw dot products are cosine similarities. The usual 1/dℓ1/\sqrt{d_{\ell}} scale produces too-uniform attention in this regime, so the canonical implementation multiplies logits by dℓd_{\ell}:

headi=softmax⁡(dℓ​qi​ki⊤)​vi.\mathrm{head}_{i}=\mathrm{softmax}\!\left(d_{\ell}\,q_{i}k_{i}^{\top}\right)v_{i}.

Standard 1/dℓ1/\sqrt{d_{\ell}} and 2​dℓ2d_{\ell} alternatives are supported as ablations. Head outputs are concatenated and projected:

CrossAttn⁡(Q,X)=Concat⁡(head1,…,headnc)​WO,WO∈ℝnc​dℓ×dℓ.\mathrm{CrossAttn}(Q,X)=\mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{head}_{1},\ldots,\mathrm{head}_{n_{c}})W_{O},\qquad W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{c}d_{\ell}\times d_{\ell}}.

Latent self-attention.

Latent self-attention uses the same expanded-head convention with nsn_{s} heads, the same QK-norm, and the same dℓd_{\ell} logit scale; no RoPE is applied:

SelfAttn⁡(Z)=Concat⁡(head1,…,headns)​WO(sa).\mathrm{SelfAttn}(Z)=\mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{head}_{1},\ldots,\mathrm{head}_{n_{s}})W_{O}^{(\mathrm{sa})}.

Feed-forward sublayer.

When enabled, the FFN is a two-layer GELU MLP with expansion ratio rr:

FFN⁡(x)=GELU⁡(x​W1)​W2,W1∈ℝdℓ×r​dℓ,W2∈ℝr​dℓ×dℓ.\mathrm{FFN}(x)=\mathrm{GELU}(xW_{1})W_{2},\qquad W_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\ell}\times rd_{\ell}},\quad W_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{rd_{\ell}\times d_{\ell}}.

The canonical configuration omits the FFN.

Output projections.

Let Zout∈ℝH×t×dℓZ_{\mathrm{out}}\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times t\times d_{\ell}} be the final latent state, optionally after a final RMSNorm. Three independent linear heads, shared across KV-heads within a layer, produce

Ck(h)\displaystyle C_{k}^{(h)} =Zout(h)​Wkey∈ℝt×d,\displaystyle=Z_{\mathrm{out}}^{(h)}W_{\mathrm{key}}\in\mathbb{R}^{t\times d}, (9)
Cv(h)\displaystyle C_{v}^{(h)} =Zout(h)​Wval∈ℝt×d,\displaystyle=Z_{\mathrm{out}}^{(h)}W_{\mathrm{val}}\in\mathbb{R}^{t\times d}, (10)
β(h)\displaystyle\beta^{(h)} =Zout(h)​wβ∈ℝt.\displaystyle=Z_{\mathrm{out}}^{(h)}w_{\beta}\in\mathbb{R}^{t}. (11)

The only per-KV-head parameters are the latent banks.

Optional β\beta shaping.

Two reparameterizations of β\beta are supported but disabled in the reported Still configuration. Saturation clips the bias smoothly: β←βmax​tanh⁡(β/βmax)\beta\leftarrow\beta_{\mathrm{max}}\tanh(\beta/\beta_{\mathrm{max}}) for βmax>0\beta_{\mathrm{max}}>0. Mass matching adds the uniform-attention offset log⁡(T/t)\log(T/t) motivated by Zweiger et al. [2026]; in the learnable variant, the implementation adds log⁡(x)+log⁡(T/t)\log(x)+\log(T/t) with a positive scalar xx initialized at 10−310^{-3}, so this begins as a suppressed mass-matching prior rather than as exact full mass matching. The paper-facing Still results set β=0\beta=0; the beta-enabled variants in this appendix are diagnostics of the optional channel.

Per-layer stack and mixed-attention models.

The full Still module instantiates one compactor object per transformer layer of the base model. For ordinary global-attention layers, (Ck,Cv)(C_{k},C_{v}) replace the corresponding full prefix cache in the reported configuration. For architectures with mixed global and sliding-window attention, such as Gemma-3, Still applies compaction only to global-attention layers; sliding-window layers keep their normal sliding-window cache, preserving the base model’s local-attention semantics while allowing global layers to use the compact prefix.

Canonical configuration summary.

For reference, the canonical Still configuration on Qwen3-4B used throughout the paper sets dℓ=256d_{\ell}=256, B=2B=2 blocks with cross-attention repeated in every block, nc=ns=1n_{c}=n_{s}=1 heads, no FFN, identity-style initialization (Appendix C) with RoPE-fix enabled, compactor RoPE base 1010, and the dℓd_{\ell} logit scale on QK-normed cross-attention. The reported Still results set the optional bias channel to β=0\beta=0; beta-enabled runs in the appendix are diagnostics. Only tt varies across the reported experiments.

Appendix B Compaction Pipeline Details

This appendix expands §2.2 and §2.3.

Single-pass compaction recipe.

  1. 1.

    Run the frozen base model on the prefix to obtain the full per-layer KV cache.

  2. 2.

    For each layer, select the cache entries to compact (the full prefix or, when explicitly requested, a text subrange [s,e)[s,e)).

  3. 3.

    Optionally un-rotate the selected keys with inverse RoPE (RoPE-fix).

  4. 4.

    Concatenate keys and values into X=[K;V]X=[K;V] and apply the per-layer compactor.

  5. 5.

    Optionally re-rotate the compact keys at evenly spaced output positions over the compacted range.

  6. 6.

    Splice any preserved prefix or suffix entries back with β=0\beta=0.

For paper-facing single-chunk evaluations the training-compatible layout compacts the full prefill cache used during training and places the question or continuation on the uncompressed continuation path. Preserving chat-template tokens separately changes the compact-cache geometry and is treated as a separate evaluation variant rather than the default.

Independent chunk compaction.

The implementation supports splitting a selected text range into independent chunks, compressing each chunk to tt entries, and concatenating the resulting compact chunks. This is an engineering baseline only and is not used for any paper-facing iterative result: each chunk is compressed without seeing compact summaries of earlier chunks, which is structurally different from the recurrent schedule below.

Iterative chunked compaction.

As spelled out in §2.3, the natural deployment form of iterative compaction rebuilds the model cache chunk by chunk: the model prefills a chunk using the current compact prefix as past key-values, Still compresses the resulting cache, and the next chunk is processed against that compact prefix. This matches the cache state seen during streaming inference and requires repeated LLM forward. This implementation also supports lookahead, a variant that provides a one chunk raw KV cache buffer at prefill. This is the standard procedure used by iterative results in this paper unless stated otherwise.

Bias semantics in attention.

When the optional bias channel is enabled and the frozen model attends over a compact prefix followed by any uncompacted suffix, β\beta is added to the compact-prefix logits:

Attn⁡(q,[CkKfix],[CvVfix],[β𝟎])=∑j=1texp⁡(q​Ck,j⊤/d+βj)​Cv,j+∑jexp⁡(q​Kfix,j⊤/d)​Vfix,j∑j=1texp⁡(q​Ck,j⊤/d+βj)+∑jexp⁡(q​Kfix,j⊤/d).\mathrm{Attn}\!\left(q;\,\begin{bmatrix}C_{k}\\ K_{\mathrm{fix}}\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}C_{v}\\ V_{\mathrm{fix}}\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}\beta\\ \mathbf{0}\end{bmatrix}\right)=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^{t}\exp\!\left(qC_{k,j}^{\top}/\sqrt{d}+\beta_{j}\right)C_{v,j}+\sum_{j}\exp\!\left(qK_{\mathrm{fix},j}^{\top}/\sqrt{d}\right)V_{\mathrm{fix},j}}{\sum_{j=1}^{t}\exp\!\left(qC_{k,j}^{\top}/\sqrt{d}+\beta_{j}\right)+\sum_{j}\exp\!\left(qK_{\mathrm{fix},j}^{\top}/\sqrt{d}\right)}.

Non-compact entries carry β=0\beta=0. In the Qwen implementation this is realized by extending the cache with a per-token bias channel and adding the bias inside attention for CompactedPrefixCache. Multi-token prefill uses a FlexAttention score modifier when available; generation-length queries use an equivalent SDPA fallback based on dimension augmentation.

Logical vs. physical cache length.

The compact cache separates physical cache length from logical sequence length. Physically, the prefix has only the compact entries plus any preserved uncompressed entries. Logically, newly generated or appended tokens receive RoPE phases as if the full original prefix were still present. The cache stores an offset equal to the original sequence length minus the maximum compacted prefix length, and the model adds this offset to continuation positions before computing RoPE.

Deployment accounting.

Still is a retained-cache reduction method in the implementation reported here. For single-pass compaction, the base model first prefills the original prefix and materializes the full KV cache; Still then maps that cache to a shorter CompactedPrefixCache. A serving implementation can release the original prefix cache as soon as the compact cache has been constructed, although PyTorch may keep the freed blocks in its CUDA allocator for reuse. The peak live tensor state during this transition is therefore base-model weights plus the full prefix KV cache, the compact KV cache, compactor weights, and transient compactor activations. The retained serving state after the transition is only the compact physical cache plus any generated suffix tokens.

For a transformer with LL layers, HkvH_{\mathrm{kv}} KV heads, head dimension dd, element size bb bytes, and physical cache length SS, the KV cache occupies

MKV​(S)=2​L​Hkv​d​b​SM_{\mathrm{KV}}(S)=2LH_{\mathrm{kv}}dbS

bytes, counting keys and values. For Qwen3-4B with L=36L=36, Hkv=8H_{\mathrm{kv}}=8, d=128d=128, and bf16/fp16 KV tensors, this is about 144144 KiB per token: 1.1251.125 GiB at 88k tokens, 4.54.5 GiB at 3232k, 9.09.0 GiB at 6464k, and 18.018.0 GiB at 128128k. The same formula with S=KS=K gives the compact-cache footprint; for example, K=328K=328 stores about 4646 MiB of KV state. The canonical Qwen3-4B compactor at t=128t=128 adds roughly 5050M parameters, about 1%1\% of the base model and about 9595 MiB in bf16.

This accounting is about retained memory rather than production serving measurements. Because subsequent tokens attend to the physical cache length KK, not the logical prefix length TT, Still reduces the retained KV state and the attention operand size after compaction. The single-pass path still includes the full prefill before the compactor forward, so the result should be read as cache-state reduction rather than elimination of the initial full-context pass. Finally, the reported Still results set the optional bias channel to β=0\beta=0. Enabling additive β\beta in production requires attention-kernel support or a custom attention path; the current repo implements it in a patched HF/PyTorch path, not as an unmodified vLLM or FlashAttention feature.

B.1 vLLM cache-injection microbenchmark

To check that the accounting above corresponds to an executable serving path, we implemented a vLLM 0.11.0 prototype for Qwen3-4B on a single NVIDIA H200. The prototype includes a standard full-cache vLLM row and compact-cache rows that allocate only KK physical prefix slots in vLLM’s paged KV cache, copy compact K/V tensors into those slots, and decode the continuation in vLLM. During compact-cache decode, the physical cache length is KK, while the RoPE positions are offset by T−KT-K, matching the logical prefix semantics described above. The Still row injects Still’s synthesized Ck,CvC_{k},C_{v}; the KV-Distill row injects the selected K/V rows produced by the corrected KV-Distill LoRA/scorer checkpoint. Both compact rows intentionally omit β\beta: they test concrete vLLM K/V injection, not the optional additive-bias diagnostic.

At this single-request setting, compact-cache serving is not an end-to-end latency win because the prototype still pays the full prefill and an out-of-band cache construction and copy step; under these measured single-turn conditions there is therefore no latency break-even point to report. The retained serving state is the intended advantage: both compact rows retain 0.1800.180 GiB of K/V state, compared with 9.09.0 GiB for the full 64k cache, and reduce the measured prototype peak allocation from 121.4121.4 GiB to 57.457.4 GiB while decoding from injected compact caches at roughly the same post-first-token throughput as full-cache vLLM. A production batching, concurrency, or sparse-kernel comparison would require a scheduler-level integration beyond this cache-injection microbenchmark.

Appendix C Identity-Style Initialization

Random initialization makes the untrained compactor far from a pass-through cache, which makes it difficult to isolate bugs in RoPE handling, optional β\beta injection, and cache integration during early training. Still therefore supports an identity-style initialization that makes the compactor a near-pass-through map at t=Tt=T. This is a diagnostic and training-stabilization device, not an exact algebraic identity for all inputs.

Construction.

The construction requires dℓ=2​dd_{\ell}=2d. In the single-cross-head case, the value projection and cross-attention output projection are initialized as identity maps over the concatenated [K;V][K;V] representation. The output heads extract the key and value halves:

Wkey=[Id​ 0],Wval=[0​Id],wβ=0.W_{\mathrm{key}}=[I_{d}\;0],\qquad W_{\mathrm{val}}=[0\;I_{d}],\qquad w_{\beta}=0.

For multiple cross-attention heads, this identity path is placed in the first expanded head; the remaining expanded heads are initialized so that they do not contribute at step zero.

Query/key pathway.

The query/key pathway is initialized so that cross-attention is dominated by relative position rather than content. With biased identity initialization the latent bank is zeroed, the cross-attention key projection is zeroed, and query and key biases are aligned to a fixed unit direction. After QK-norm, the unrotated query and key directions are therefore nearly constant, and the compactor’s internal RoPE is the main signal distinguishing positions. With a small RoPE base (1010 in the canonical configuration), this produces a sharply local, block-diagonal attention pattern when the latent positions tile the input range. At t<Tt<T, each latent reads from a local region rather than a single token.

Refinement sublayers as residual identities.

To avoid disturbing the initial pass-through path, the self-attention output projections, FFN second layers, and any later cross-attention output projections are zero-initialized. These refinement sublayers therefore begin as residual identities and become active only as their output projections train away from zero.

Let LL, HH, dd be the base model’s layer count, KV-head count, and KV head dimension; let the compactor have latent dimension dℓd_{\ell}, compact length tt, BB blocks, ncn_{c} cross-attention heads, nsn_{s} self-attention heads, and FFN expansion ratio rr. Let BcB_{c} be the number of blocks containing cross-attention: Bc=1B_{c}=1 for the Perceiver-resampler setting and Bc=BB_{c}=B when cross-attention is repeated every block. Ignoring small optional biases, the per-layer parameter count is

pℓ\displaystyle p_{\ell} =H​t​dℓ⏟latent bank+Bc​(2​nc​dℓ2+4​d​nc​dℓ)⏟cross-attention\displaystyle=\underbrace{Htd_{\ell}}_{\text{latent bank}}+B_{c}\underbrace{\left(2n_{c}d_{\ell}^{2}+4dn_{c}d_{\ell}\right)}_{\text{cross-attention}}
+B​(4​ns​dℓ2)⏟self-attention+B​(2​r​dℓ2)⏟FFN, if enabled+(2​dℓ​d+dℓ)⏟output heads.\displaystyle+B\underbrace{\left(4n_{s}d_{\ell}^{2}\right)}_{\text{self-attention}}+B\underbrace{\left(2rd_{\ell}^{2}\right)}_{\text{FFN, if enabled}}+\underbrace{\left(2d_{\ell}d+d_{\ell}\right)}_{\text{output heads}}.

Disabled sublayers drop their term. The total parameter count is L​pℓLp_{\ell}.

For Qwen3-4B with L=36L=36, H=8H=8, d=128d=128, the canonical configuration (t=128,dℓ=256,B=2,nc=ns=1,(t=128,d_{\ell}=256,B=2,n_{c}=n_{s}=1, repeated cross-attention, no FFN)) has approximately 5050M parameters, around 1%1\% of the base model. Larger illustrative configurations include (t=140,dℓ=256,B=4,nc=ns=8,r=4)(t=140,d_{\ell}=256,B=4,n_{c}=n_{s}=8,r=4) at approximately 466466M parameters with first-block-only cross-attention or 692692M with cross-attention repeated in every block.
